title: `resultType`
description: The discriminator now required on every result, distinguishing a completed result from one that needs more input.
question: Does the framework read the result discriminator before using a result?
why: A client that ignores `resultType` will treat an `input_required` result as a finished one and hand the agent a half-finished answer. Results from older servers that omit the field must be read as complete, so tolerant parsing is part of the requirement.
known_issues: Measured by scripts/measure_protocol.py: each adapter runs against fixtures/base_protocol_server.py behind the wire recorder, and the cell is read from the captures.

notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: an `input_required` result is refused as unfinished by `MCPServer.callTool` (the client throws `Cannot fulfil input request`), but on the agent path the tool's default error function turns that throw into ordinary output, so the model receives "An error occurred while running the tool..." as a completed result.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: an `input_required` result is not surfaced as one: with no elicitation handler the call fails, and the Function hands the agent the text `MCP tool 'needs_input' failed: Elicitation not supported...` as an ordinary result.
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: depends on the boundary. With no elicitation handler on the session, `Tool.acall` raises `MCPError: Elicitation not supported` and the call is refused as unfinished. `dspy.ReAct` turns that into an `Execution error in needs_input:` traceback the model reads as a completed observation.
notes.copilot_sdk: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): depends on the boundary, measured with no elicitation handler set. `session.rpc.tools.execute` refuses an `input_required` result as unfinished ("tools/call requested elicitation input but no elicitation responder is wired"). On the agent path the same failure reaches the provider as an ordinary `tool` message, which the model reads as a completed result.
